quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When you see a red traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are coming.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A red traffic light means you must stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on a red light if there is no sign that says you cannot.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow light mean?

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns you that a red light is coming soon. Slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through with care.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you drive. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine.
Turn on your hazard lights and prepare for impact.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe spot, and stop.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe spot, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, you need to use extra strength to steer. Reduce your speed and pull off the road to a safe place to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. Do not turn around at this location.

questions.question: How do you enter a freeway correctly?

options.text: Signal, let other traffic go first, and merge at the same speed as traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can watch the traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, let other traffic go first, and merge at the same speed as traffic.
questions.explanation: Signal and merge at the same speed as other traffic. Always let other traffic go first when entering a roadway.

questions.question: What is a speed restriction sign?

options.text: You can ignore it when it is raining, snowing, or icy.
It has a triangle shape.
It is blue with black letters.
It shows a recommended speed for curves or turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: It shows a recommended speed for curves or turns.
questions.explanation: Warning signs for curves and turns often show a recommended speed. Even if you feel safe going faster in good weather, never do so in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who goes first?

options.text: The driver who arrived first.
The driver who arrived last.
One driver should go without stopping.
One driver should wave others to go ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrived first.
questions.explanation: All drivers must stop at a four-way stop. The driver who reaches the intersection first goes first. If two drivers arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: Your right wheels leave the pavement. What do you do?

options.text: Stop quickly.
Pull completely off the road and get back on when safe.
Speed up and steer back on the road fast.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then gently steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: Stay calm. Release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and gently guide your vehicle back onto the road. Use both hands on the wheel and make a small turn. Check for other traffic before steering back.

questions.question: What is a good rule for passing other cars?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever you can.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Get to the front of slow traffic to see better.
Always flash your lights and honk to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Passing increases the risk of a crash. If you drive faster than traffic, you will need to keep passing. Drive with traffic flow, within the speed limit, and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop?

options.text: Signal lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
Road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions.
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect how well you can stop. Reduce your speed on poor roads to stay in control. Driving too fast on slippery or wet roads makes stopping harder and more dangerous.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, what is safest?

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than other cars.
Drive slower than other cars.
Drive at the same speed as other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other cars.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other cars. Always drive at the same speed as traffic around you, but do not exceed the speed limit.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Very uncommon.
Very dangerous.
Not a serious problem.
Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Very dangerous.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers at risk. Paying attention to the road helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: You have done enough.
Wait for police to arrive.
Leave a written note with your name, address, and details of the accident.
You can leave.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and details of the accident.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car, try to find the owner. If you cannot, leave a written note with your name, address, and what happened.

questions.question: Before you start your car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have seat belts on.
Make sure only adults have seat belts on.
Make sure only children have seat belts on.
Make sure everyone in the car has seat belts on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure everyone in the car has seat belts on.
questions.explanation: Make it a habit to buckle your seat belt and check that all passengers do the same before you start driving.

questions.question: Does drinking coffee after alcohol help you sober up?

options.text: Yes, it lowers blood alcohol level.
Yes, it cancels the alcohol.
No, it has no effect on blood alcohol level.
No, it raises blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it has no effect on blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Drinking coffee will not lower your blood alcohol level. It may help you stay awake, but it cannot make you sober.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Two-way left turn.
Two-way traffic.
Minimum speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: One-way traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you which direction traffic must go on a one-way street.

questions.question: When you turn or change lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if no other cars are around.
Signal only if other cars are nearby.
Signal only at night.
Signal only at night in heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if no other cars are around.
questions.explanation: Always signal when you change lanes, turn, or pull away from the curb. Make this a habit every time.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private driveway?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other drivers.
Stick part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to merge with traffic.
Let pedestrians and traffic on the roadway go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians and traffic on the roadway go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a private driveway, you must let pedestrians and cars on the roadway go first.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: The speed limit is now 20 mph.
A lower speed zone is starting.
More pedestrians may be around.
The lower speed zone is ending.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lower speed zone is ending.
questions.explanation: Follow the school zone speed limit when signs show you are in one. The "End school zone" sign marks where the lower speed zone ends.

questions.question: In bad weather, drivers should:

options.text: Speed up to reach their destination faster.
Follow other cars more closely.
Stay farther behind other cars.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: In wet weather, increase the space between your car and the car ahead of you.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Hunting area.
State park.
Deer crossing.
Wildlife preserve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Deer crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that deer cross the road in this area. You should slow down, watch carefully, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They have large blind spots.
They can stop faster than passenger vehicles.
They need less room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, on the sides, and in back. Do not stay in these areas. Trucks need more space to turn and stop than regular cars because of their size and weight.

questions.question: What should you adjust first when you get into a car to drive?

options.text: Your seat belt
The steering wheel
Your rearview mirror
Your seat

questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat
questions.explanation: Adjust your seat first so you are comfortable and can see the road clearly. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel based on your seat position.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger signals you, or when you see a stop sign or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Some railroad crossings do not have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street the wrong way.
U-turns are not allowed.
You can go if the way is clear.
You must stop completely before going forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street the wrong way.
questions.explanation: If you drive past these signs, you are going the wrong direction and could have a head-on crash. Turn around carefully.

questions.question: When passing a parked vehicle, you should:

options.text: Be ready for someone or a vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to give you the right of way.
Honk your horn to warn drivers and pedestrians.
Speed up to avoid pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for someone or a vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep distance between your car and parked vehicles. A person may step out of a parked car or from between vehicles, or a car may suddenly start to pull out.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: One-way road.
No right turn allowed.
Exit.
Sharp right turn ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp right turn ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that there is a sharp right turn in the road ahead.

questions.question: When can you honk your horn?

options.text: When you need to brake quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you lose control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you lose control of your car.
questions.explanation: One good time to use your horn is if you lose control of your vehicle. Sound your horn to alert other drivers of the danger.

questions.question: Looking over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes, leaving a curb, or merging into traffic is:

options.text: A bad driving habit.
A good driving habit.
Not needed.
Not needed if you use your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: A good driving habit.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder toward the next lane. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: You reach an intersection blocked by traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move slowly until traffic ahead clears.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Stay out of the intersection until you can drive all the way through.
Use your horn to make cars move forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until you can drive all the way through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if traffic is blocked on the other side and you cannot get completely through. Wait until traffic clears so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign show?

options.text: A right turn.
An intersection.
A lane change.
A road curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: An intersection.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a T intersection is ahead.

questions.question: At night, how should you look to reduce glare from oncoming headlights?

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Look at the right side of the road ahead. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights because the glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not brake right away.
Slow down gradually and pull off the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, take your foot off the gas. Do not brake immediately. Slow down gradually, then gently apply the brakes and pull off the side of the road.

questions.question: When you see a steady green traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Continue driving unless vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving unless vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, let pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection go first. You may continue, but be ready to slow down or stop if the light changes.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Stay farther away from the vehicles in front of you.
Drive carefully near all vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In snow, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase your distance from other vehicles because slippery roads need more stopping distance.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickest when they are:

options.text: Flat.
Curvy.
In the sun.
Shaded.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shaded.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze faster than sunny areas. These spots take the longest to dry in cold or wet weather.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Hazard flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams bounce off the fog and reduce your vision even more.

questions.question: When may you exceed the speed limit?

options.text: When passing another vehicle.
Never.
Where there are no police officers.
On country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You cannot exceed the speed limit at any time, including when passing. Always follow the legal speed limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic signal ahead shows a red light.
The traffic signal ahead is broken.
The traffic signal ahead shows a green light.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is at the next intersection.

questions.question: When a bus signals to re-enter the roadway after stopping, what must you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Move to the left lane.
Yield.
Speed up to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any bus that is signaling to return to the main road. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus merge safely.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You do not have to stop completely.
Driving conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion while driving?

options.text: Only behind your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of your vehicle.
All around your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: All around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space all around your vehicle so you have time to react to danger. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your sides.

questions.question: When turning right, where should your car be positioned?

options.text: Near the center of the street.
Close to the left side of the street.
Close to the right side of the street.
Past the center of the intersection when starting the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Close to the right side of the street.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, move to the far right side of the road. Never cut across other lanes to make a turn.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Use a different route.
Drive the same as you would on dry roads.
Stay farther behind other vehicles.
Avoid bridges and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between you and the car ahead. Your vehicle needs more time to stop on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with flashing signals?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing signals at a railroad crossing, stop at least 15 feet away from the tracks. Look and listen for trains. Also watch for lowered crossing gates.

questions.question: You are angry from something at work. When you get to your car, what should you do?

options.text: Turn up the radio so you stop thinking about it.
Drive fast to release your anger.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Have a few drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, wait until you feel calm before driving. Driving while emotional is dangerous to you and others.

questions.question: How should you use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before you enter the exit ramp.
Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep the same speed once in the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic in the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until you are on the exit ramp. Then reduce your speed.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: Tires become less effective as you drive faster.
Good tires are not affected by water.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
The road becomes more slippery when you slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires become less effective as you drive faster.
questions.explanation: As you drive faster on wet roads, your tires lose grip. If you go too fast, your tires will slide on the water and you will hydroplane.

questions.question: When can you cross solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass other traffic going the same direction.
Only during the day.
Anytime.
When you are turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are turning.
questions.explanation: You can cross broken lines, but not solid yellow lines. The only time you can cross a solid yellow line is when you are turning.

questions.question: Where may you not park?

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the road edge.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the curb.
